name: Volar approach to the metacarpophalangeal joint
aliases: palmar approach to the MCP joint
corridor: Volar Z-incision over the MCP joint through the A1 pulley region, retracting the flexor tendons to reach the volar plate and joint, protecting the collateral digital nerves

positioning.text: Position supine with the hand on a hand table under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the MCP joint level and the palmar skin creases.

incision.text: Make a Z-shaped incision over the MCP joint with the apex radial or ulnar at a skin crease, extending proximally in Z-fashion along the creases to avoid contracture.

superficial_interval.text: Expose the flexor retinaculum and A1 pulley and identify the collateral neurovascular bundles, remembering the digital nerve may be displaced volarly with the metacarpal head after dislocation.

deep_interval.text: Sharply dissect the flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus off the volar plate and capsule and retract them to expose the volar joint.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with collateral digital nerves, flexor retinaculum and A1 pulley, flexor tendons, volar plate, and the MCP joint.

structures_at_risk.text: The collateral neurovascular bundles of the digit and the common digital nerve are at risk, especially when a nerve is displaced volarly with the metacarpal head.

danger_zones.text: The volar-displaced metacarpal head region is the danger zone because the digital nerve can be draped over it.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid overretraction to prevent nerve damage and keep multiple incisions spaced to prevent skin flap ischemia.

exposure.text: Exposes the volar MCP joint and any interposed ruptured capsule after dislocation.

limitations.text: The volar approach gives limited access to the dorsal joint and depends on careful digital nerve identification.

indications.text: Indicated for irreducible volar MCP dislocation and selected volar MCP joint pathology.

closure.text: Repair the joint capsule with fine sutures, reposition the flexor tendons, and do not repair the A1 pulley to avoid tendon sheath contracture.

complications.text: Complications include digital nerve injury, skin flap ischemia, and MCP stiffness.

procedure_applications.condition: An irreducible volar MCP dislocation or metacarpal head fracture needs open volar access

questions.question: Why is a Z-shaped incision used over the MCP joint?
questions.answer: To respect the skin creases and avoid contracture.

questions.question: Why is the A1 pulley not repaired at closure?
questions.answer: Because repair may cause tendon sheath contracture and restrict flexor excursion.

questions.question: Where may the digital nerve lie after a volar MCP dislocation?
questions.answer: Displaced volarly, draped over the metacarpal head.
